findings.location: paper/make_gulls_macros.py:151 (bmlGullsMeanRec*) and :220 (bmlGullsColUndetOne); used at draft 84216cb:174-175 and :224
findings.claim: Every number is 'rounded ONCE from exact counts where the artifact has them'.
findings.actual: Two values in the text are rounded twice and come out wrong. The artifacts store 4-decimal values and the generator re-rounds them to 3 decimals. bmlGullsMeanRecFspl prints 0.538, but the exact trapezoid mean recall is 0.538539, which rounds to 0.539 (the artifact stores 0.5385). bmlGullsColUndetOne prints 0.170, but the exact rate is 383/2260 = 0.16947, which rounds to 0.169 (the artifact stores 0.1695, and Python's format(0.1695,'.3f') gives '0.170'). Both errors are still in the working tree.
findings.how_checked: MeanRec: recomputed the trapezoid integral of 1S2L recall over single-lens FA <= 0.3 from the raw rows (the same 4-decimal threshold grid). ColUndet: rebuilt the 6,600-event truth subset from gulls_truth_cache_v2 (label policy reproduces label_detect with 0 mismatches), matched the F146-only threshold at the 5.2% budget on the 1,600 singles (thr 0.8838), and counted k=383 of 2,260 undetectable binaries. All other 4-dp to 3-dp macros were checked and are correct.
findings.fix: Have the reducers store k (or unrounded values) for these quantities, or round from full precision. At minimum, use n_undetectable x rate to recover k for the colour-ablation rates.
findings.verdict_note: MeanRec: I reran summarise()'s trapezoid on the raw rows (scratch m4a.py). Scores are stored at 4 dp, so the 4-dp threshold grid is exact. fspl5s_g08 comes out at 0.538539, which rounds once to 0.539; the artifact stores 0.5385 and the macro prints 0.538 (Python formats 0.5385 as 0.538). It is the only one of the 15 models that differs. ColUndet: I rebuilt the set from gulls_truth_cache_v2 label_detect (6,600 events; 2,740 detectable and 2,260 undetectable binaries), matched the F146-only threshold at 5.2% (thr 0.8838, FA 0.0519), and got k=383, so 383/2260 = 0.16947, which rounds to 0.169; the macro is 0.170. With n=2260, k=383 is also the only integer consistent with the stored 0.1695. A boundary scan of every formatter input found one more case: bmlMsDetHostPlanet prints 50, but 0.505 x 598 = 302/598 = 50.50%, which rounds to 51; that macro is unused in the draft. Caveat: the docstring says 'rounded ONCE from exact counts where the artifact has them', and these artifacts store no counts, so this breaks the spirit of the contract rather than its letter. Both errors are one unit in the third decimal; severity is closer to minor than major.

findings.claim: The combined arm's differences are 'less than the 0.014-0.023 by which two runs of one recipe differ'. Elsewhere: 'Two fine-tunes with the same recipe on different pools differ by 0.014-0.023 ... differences of that size between single-seed checkpoints are not resolved'.
findings.actual: bmlSeedSpread compares sched_rand with ft_g08e12. Both used the same seed (--seed 20260823 in schedule_finetune_local.py COMMON and in modal_gap_finetune.py), so this is not a seed replicate. The pools differ in size: g08e12 used 6 train shards (~45k events, REVISION.md line 116), sched_rand 12 shards (89,919 events, cadence_local_work/work15/mm_train/meta.json). Twelve epochs therefore means twice as many optimizer steps for sched_rand. Line 199 also drops 'on different pools'. Supporting evidence from the uncommitted working tree: the smooth-magnification control (same seed, near-identical pool) reproduces fspl5s_g08 to within 0.0011 in recall and 0.0008 per rho/|u0| bin. So the 0.014-0.023 spread reflects pool and length differences, not run-to-run noise.
findings.how_checked: Recomputed the spread from rows (|dRecall| = 0.0142 / 0.0199 / 0.0232 at 2 / 5.2 / 11.7%), read both runners' arguments and the pool metadata, and computed espl vs fspl5s from rows_full_fspl5s_espl_g08.json.
findings.fix: Describe it as 'two fine-tunes of the same recipe on different pools (45k vs 90k events, same seed)' in both places, and do not call it run-to-run or seed variation. Better, get a true seed replicate before using it to declare differences unresolved.
findings.verdict_note: Both checkpoints record seed 20260823 (ft_g08e12.pt and ft_sched_rand.pt, loaded on CPU; the same seed also appears in modal_gap_finetune.py:100 and schedule_finetune_local.py:70), and both were saved at best-validation epoch 8. The pools differ: cadence_local_work/work15/mm_train/meta.json has n_events 89,919, while REVISION.md:116 gives 45k for g08e12, consistent with 6 x 7,479-event shards. I could not open the Modal volume to confirm that pool. The spread from raw rows is 0.0142 / 0.0198 / 0.0233 at 2 / 5.2 / 11.7%, which gives the macros 0.014 / 0.023. At HEAD, draft:203 still says 'two runs of one recipe' without 'on different pools'; draft:218 keeps the qualifier. REVISION rows 13 and 14 and the macro name call it a 'seed spread'. Same-pool, same-seed pairs differ far less: espl vs fspl5s by at most 0.0011 in recall and 0.0008 per bin, and sched_rand vs sched_rand_norelabel by 0.0086 / 0.0043 / 0.0013. Same-seed pairs share an RNG stream, though, so no true seed-variance estimate exists either way.

findings.claim: Control vs finite source: 'The physics acts where the diagnosis predicts ... while the point-like bins barely change'
findings.actual: In rate terms the rho/|u0| < 0.1 bins change little (0.036 to 0.031 and 0.048 to 0.037). In counts, though, they supply 190 (654 to 563, 419 to 320) of the 506 false alarms removed between the control and fspl5s, 38% of the reduction, in bins where finite-source effects are negligible. findings.fix: State the rate change in the point-like bins, and note that part of the drop occurs where finite size cannot matter.
findings.verdict_note: The numbers reproduce from raw rows. Control to fspl5s, per-bin k: 654/419/330/362/221/137 to 563/320/238/268/151/77, a reduction of 91/99/92/94/70/60 (total 506). Rates in those bins go 0.036 to 0.031 and 0.048 to 0.037 (relative -14% and -24%), so 'barely change' holds in absolute rate but not clearly in relative terms. However, the control is a single-factor comparison (same pool shape, warm start, recipe and seed), so attributing the 6.4% to 4.8% drop to the training-set physics is valid by design. What the counts undercut is the mechanism reading ('acts where the diagnosis predicts'), not the causal attribution, and there is no seed replicate to size the <0.1-bin changes. The same 'concentrated in the two largest bins' wording is in REVISION row 13, VERIFICATION G14 and CHANGELOG:24, where those bins hold only 130 of the 506 removed alarms (26%). findings.actual: The draft's own control contradicts this (lines 170-176; ledger row 13, CHANGELOG and G14 all say 'extra training explains most, physics the rest'). Single-lens false-alarm counts are g08e12 3,885 -> pspl5s_ctrl 2,123 -> fspl5s 1,617. The physics therefore removes 506 of g08e12's residual false alarms, which is 13% of them and 22% of the total reduction. Of those 506, 190 fall in bins with rho/|u0| < 0.1, where finite-source deviations are sub-mmag, and only 130 in the two largest-ratio bins, so 'point-like bins barely change' understates it. The recall part is not resolved either. fspl5s minus control at the 2% budget is 0.021, inside the draft's own 'not resolved' spread of 0.014-0.023 (lines 216-218). Under event-rate weighting it is -0.015 / +0.010 / +0.012 at the three budgets, and every bootstrap 95% CI includes 0 (see the next finding).
findings.how_checked: Per-bin k/n from transfer_tradeoff_all.json (ft_g08e12, pspl5s_ctrl_g08, fspl5s_g08). Recalls from the artifact and recomputed from rmdc26_scores.csv.gz. Weighted bootstrap with 300 resamples of events, script at scratchpad/reverify/draft-logic/wboot.py.
findings.fix: Line 361-362: 'that continued training on a pool rich in high-magnification single lenses removed most of the remaining single-lens false alarms, and finite-source single lenses removed a further 1.6 points, most strongly (relative to the rate) in the largest rho/|u0| bins'. Drop 'a large part' at 183-184. At 173, say the recall gain from physics is at or below the run-to-run spread. In the abstract, do not imply that the finite-source step produced the drop.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced the false-alarm counts: g08e12 3885, control 2123, fspl5s 1617. The physics accounts for 506 of them: 13.0% of g08e12's residual and 22.3% of the total reduction. Per bin (control minus fspl5s) it is 91/99/92/94/70/60, so 190 fall at rho/|u0|<0.1 and 130 in the top two bins. That conflicts with 'a large part' at :183-184 and :361-362. It also conflicts with CHANGELOG and G14 ('extra training explains most'); G57's 'a large part' fix predates the control. 'Point-like bins barely change' holds in absolute rate (<0.03 bin 0.036->0.031) but not in counts or relative terms (-14%/-24%). The recall sub-claim is only partly right. Unweighted, fspl5s minus control is 0.021/0.029/0.048 at 2/5.2/11.7%, inside the 0.014-0.023 spread only at 2%; at the quoted 5.2% it is 1.3x the top of the spread. So 'at or below spread' is wrong unweighted and holds only under weights: -0.015/+0.010/+0.012, with 400-resample CIs all including 0 (f3d.py). New: within tE strata, fspl5s's edge over the control sits in the 1-10 d events at every rho/|u0|, and the >3 bin is 70% tE<3 d (f3h.py). This further weakens 'acts where the diagnosis predicts'.

findings.claim: The headline and the decisions use unweighted rates on RMDC26's sample: FA 4.8%, recall at the 5.2% budget 0.295 -> 0.390, 'the physics then takes them to ... 0.390', and a combined arm 'within 0.008 at every budget' so that 'the two gains do not add'. The draft gives rate-weighted numbers only for sub-day FA and the cascade prevalence.
findings.actual: RMDC26's unweighted single lenses are dominated by short events: 37.9% have tE < 3 d, against 15.6% rate-weighted, 3.4% and 1.9% of the planetary classes, and 1.8% of our training prior's mass. Median tE is 4.3 d for single lenses and 13.5 d for 1S2L. fspl5s's false-alarm rate rises with tE: 3.1%, 3.9%, 7.6% and 12.2% in the 1-3, 3-10, 10-30 and 30-300 d bins. Its rate-weighted FA is 7.6% (unweighted 4.8%), and 2.8% at 0.957 (unweighted 1.6%). With RMDC26 final_weight applied, 1S2L recall at the 2 / 5.2 / 11.7% budgets is: g08e12 0.233/0.336/0.482; control 0.273/0.374/0.517; fspl5s 0.257/0.383/0.529; combined 0.282/0.408/0.546. The fspl5s gain over g08e12 halves (+0.047 at 5.2%). fspl5s minus control is -0.015/+0.010/+0.012, with bootstrap CIs that include 0. The combined arm leads fspl5s by +0.025/+0.024/+0.017, with CIs that exclude 0 and exceed the stated 0.014-0.023 spread. With the budget set inside tE strata of 10 d or more (63% of 1S2L), fspl5s does not beat g08e12 (0.353 vs 0.363 and 0.378 vs 0.396).
findings.how_checked: Joined validation/gulls/rmdc26_scores.csv.gz with /tmp/rmdc26_meta.parquet (weight equals final_weight to 5e-6, tE equals tE_ref). Computed weighted thresholds and recalls, tE-stratified matched budgets, and an event bootstrap (ESS 8,309 single lenses, 2,841 1S2L). The training-prior mass comes from priors.py (TE_MEDIAN 16.3 d, sigma 0.35 dex, [1,300] d).
findings.fix: Report rate-weighted FA and matched-budget recall next to the unweighted values, or justify the unweighted sample. Add the tE mismatch to the out-of-support paragraph. Re-state the physics attribution and the combined-arm 'tie' / 'do not add' conclusions (and the rationale for keeping fspl5s in ledger row 14) as dependent on the weighting, or rerun the decision under the weights.
findings.verdict_note: Every number reproduces (f3a-g.py). Joining the scores to the meta table gives weight=final_weight and tE=tE_ref to 5e-6. For single lenses, tE<3 d is 37.9% unweighted and 15.6% weighted; for the planetary classes 3.4%/1.9%; prior mass 1.76%. Median tE is 4.31 d for 1S1L and 13.51 d for 1S2L. fspl5s FA by tE is 3.1/3.9/7.6/12.2%. Weighted FA is 7.57% (the committed transfer_full_reduced_fspl5s_g08.json also has 0.0757) and 2.81% at 0.957. Weighted 1S2L recall matches the finding exactly for all four models. Combined minus fspl5s is +0.025/+0.024/+0.017, CIs [0.002,0.042]/[0.010,0.043]/[0.001,0.031]. They exclude 0, but the lower bounds do not exceed 0.014-0.023, so that sub-claim is overstated. However, the weighted analogue of the seed-spread proxy (|sched_rand-g08e12|) is only 0.002/0.005/0.004, and on 2S2L the lead is +0.036/+0.045/+0.025. 'Do not add' therefore flips under weighting. tE-stratified at 5.2%: 10-30 d 0.353 vs 0.363, 30-300 d 0.378 vs 0.396. Pooled over strata, g08e12/control/fspl5s give 0.320/0.330/0.326 (combined 0.352): the unweighted 0.295->0.390 gain comes almost entirely from short-tE single lenses (g08e12 flags 14.1% at 1-3 d, fspl5s 3.1%). Severity is arguably major, not critical: the numbers are correct for the unweighted sample, but that choice is undisclosed and conclusions depend on it.

findings.claim: 'Recall is limited by significance rather than amplitude'.
findings.actual: The claim is true, but no committed artifact supports it. The artifact stores only 1D marginals, and its amplitude marginal also rises steeply (0.40, 0.42, 0.51, 0.65, 0.85 across the 0.02 to >0.5 mag bins), which on its face contradicts 'rather than amplitude'. My 2D recomputation supports the claim: at fixed dchi2 1e4-1e5, recall across amplitude bins is 0.89/0.76/0.65/0.65/0.84; at fixed amplitude 0.02-0.05 mag it rises 0.18 -> 0.31 -> 0.48 -> 0.89 -> 1.00 across dchi2 bins.
findings.how_checked: Read the transfer_detectability_relabel.json marginals. Built the 2D table from gulls_truth_cache_v2 records (first 2,500 per class, 2,740 claimable) joined to fspl5s scores; the frozen recall 0.5146 reproduces the artifact.
findings.fix: Store the 2D breakdown in the reducer's artifact and cite it, or write 'recall tracks significance more closely than amplitude'.
findings.verdict_note: transfer_detectability_relabel.json fspl5s_g08 stores only 1D marginals. By amplitude: 0.397/0.424/0.510/0.651/0.846, where the median dchi2 per bin rises from 920 to 328k, i.e. confounded. By dchi2: 0.172 to 0.866. I rebuilt the 2D table from gulls_truth_cache_v2 with the documented first-N selection (6600 records, 2740 claimable), joined to the fspl5s scores (f11.py). Frozen recall 0.5146 reproduces the artifact. At dchi2 1e4-1e5, recall by amplitude is 0.89/0.76/0.65/0.65/0.84. At amplitude 0.02-0.05 it rises 0.18/0.31/0.48/0.89/1.00 across dchi2 bins. A linear probability fit gives coefficients +0.218 on log dchi2 and -0.045 on log amp. So the claim is true, but no committed artifact supports it (G39 stored only the 1D dchi2 marginal).
